title: Positional Information
interviewAnswer: Attention itself is permutation-invariant, so transformers need positional information. Systems may use learned embeddings, sinusoidal encodings or relative/rotary approaches such as RoPE.
why: Attention alone is permutation-equivariant, so transformers need a way to represent order or relative position.
intuition: Without position information, the same set of token embeddings in a different order would look equivalent to pure self-attention.
deepDive: Absolute learned/sinusoidal embeddings add a position vector to each token. Relative position methods encode pairwise distance; rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) rotate query/key dimensions based on position and support relative-phase behavior. Position methods affect length extrapolation and long-context performance.
math: Sinusoidal PE uses sin/cos at different frequencies; RoPE applies position-dependent rotations to Q/K pairs.
workedExample: “dog bites man” and “man bites dog” contain the same words but different order; position information lets attention distinguish them.
commonMistakes: Saying attention inherently knows sequence order.
Treating all positional encodings as interchangeable for arbitrary context extension.
Changing maximum context without checking positional-training limits.
followUps: How does long-context extension interact with position encodings?
production: Long-context serving must respect the model’s positional method/training range; naive extension can degrade quality even if memory allows more tokens.
